text: Breathing and kicking are two of the most important parts of swimming. A swimming stroke takes about 10-15 seconds. The first part is a downward flow of air into the lungs, which sends out a flow of air and water. The water is sucked in through the lungs, into the upper chest cavity and into the lower chest cavity. The second part is the lift of the feet and the stroke, which takes about 10-15 seconds. The second part is the lift of the head and the stroke, which takes about 2-3 seconds. The third part is the lift of the torso and the stroke, which takes about 2-3 seconds. The third part is the lift of the arms and the stroke, which takes about 2-3 seconds.
